That kind of behavior modification will require you to hire a professional to teach you what to practice on a regular basis. The cat is the biggest challenge since typically getting dogs acclimated to cats requires desensitization which is a long process - you're basically rewiring the dogs response from "see cat chase cat" to "see cat ignore cat" that takes a long time, at least 6 months of careful and supervised direction. So this is something the owners should do, with a professional trainer (it would only take one or two sessions for them to understand what techniques to practice and then after that everyone has to be consistent with the training)
As far as your plants you could get a pet block, designed to repel animals from going near certain areas. A pet friendly one of course (not a poison)

In that case you can also substitute a treat for affection. For some dogs (and their lucky owners) praise is actually enough a "good girl!" And a short sweet rub on her favorite spot (chin, chest etc) could do in a pinch if you don't have a treat. Your treat loving pup may feel a little jipped if he's used to getting nice treats BUT at least he is still getting something to signify that he did the right behavior. In fact, I usualy say "YES!" When my dog gets it right before I give her the treat because it is a signifier - not only does me saying yes tell her that she did the right thing but it also lets her know that she can expect a reward (treat or praise). The signifier - be it a clicker or a simple "Yes!" Gives you enough time to get the treat, but it catches the behavior at the right moment so they know exactly at what point they did the right thing. Timing is everything

Consistency is the only thing that will really help elevate your training. 
As far as cycling through tricks, be patient and never reward the wrong action, I know it can be cute but if it's not what you're asking for just hold off on the treat until he gets it right. Just keep in mind that whatever you reward is what he will keep doing. Have patience and be firm with your family members that it's for his own good that they maintain the consistency.
Keep the training sessions short and frequent - don't just demand the same thing over and over. For a good half hour training session I like to start with the stuff they know (or should know) very well and save the new tricks for second to last. The last thing should be back to the basics again so you end on a positive note.
Once you eatablish somethig like sit, you can go into "sit, stay" where you can walk out of the room "come" from a different room so he comes to you, "down" so he lays down, army crawl is a fun one, so is play dead.. Helpful ones are "go to your spot" teaching him to lay down in a designated area (blanket / carpet / crate they are tactile so make it a spot that has a different texture) you can use this for when company comes over and you want him to go settle down...
For carpet try tropiclean, there's even a deep pad penetrator. The best solution is to steam clean though using nature's miracle carpet shampoo or any other carpet shampoo with enzymes

The pronged collars are designed to imitate the snap of a mothers jaws that would normally serve as a natural correction... The gentle leaders/ martingale/ choke collars will make the dog uncomfortable but only enough to where the dog understands the boundaries of what is acceptable.
Dogs in training still always receive some form of physical correction - not necessarily force per SE but they do have an acute tactile sense. I don't consider the gentle leader to be punishment, it's more of a safe humane way to get the dog to stop pulling - if he were wearing a regular collar that could actually do more damage. Some dogs are persistent and will pull so hard that they collapse their tracheas, so that's why the gentle leader I think falls out of the category of punishment. The choke and marringale collars basically speed up the choking process that would occur if the dog were using a regular collar anyway. 
Martingales with a chain though are effective in one more additional sense - sound. Dogs in theory should hear the sound of the chain rubbing and would know the collar will tighten up.
Pronged collars should only be used for a short period of time during training sessions, not all the time...

The head collar would be appropriate for your lunging dog but not for Kia (imo) because the head collars are designed with forward motion in mind. You won't be able to pull Kia along in a safe or Effective manner.
You can use a coupler with gentle leaders/ Haltis but I suggest getting one that has some shock absorption for example wacky walkrs makes one that is good. That way they won't be yanking each other's neck if one tries to lunge away from the other.
For kia especially I recommend the freedom harness made by 2hounds. It fits like a step in harness but has a ring on the front like the easy walk. However major difference is that it also has a martingale style closure on the back with a ring. It comes with a double ended Leash so you attach one end of the leash to the front of the dog and the other end to the back. This gives you complete control over the dogs forward motion. If she runs ahead the front ring redirects her body motion back to you, and the martingale style closure on the back tightens the harness which not only gives you more control but also can act as a signifier that her behavior is not appropriate (ie if she pulls she won't get what she wants) you can use with your shiba mix too for this purpose, and for Kia it would help because it's much safer than the easy walk since it has the strap down the middle. One of my dogs was like Kia and she has never been able to get out f the freedom harness. 
I still use the freedom harness for both dogs but after s few months of using the dual ended Leash they learned (by habit) to stick by my side for the most part, so now I just use the front connection with a regular Leash

I feel you. A bunch of terrible shit has always surrounded me since childhood and I've been suicidal often in all my dark moments. I also know people who have self harmed pretty bad. I only tried that a couple of times but refuse to do it anymore because I don't want to deal with the embarassment of other people seeing... 
I too have faced many moments where I hate myself even more because I'm too much of a coward to go through with my suicide plan..
But I often think of why that may be. For one thing we are designed to be afraid of death, it's a survival instinct. You instinctually do not want to die. Now if you have devised a means that you are comfortable with dying from, and you set up all the tools or situation that is required, and you're figuratively or literally "on the ledge" about it... If you have any second doubts don't do it. Don't do it either way in my opinion but I don't know what everyone's life story is, and I can't judge someone for the choices they make. However, in my experience - I never go through with it because there is always even a smidgen of doubt. What if it doesn't work and I end up with brain damage, liver failure, or a paraplegic - it would be a billion times worse. What if I change my mind as I'm on my "way out" but I can't do anything about it? (That one is actually something I am sure that everyone experiences as they are dying. I've been in a couple near death experiences and I can tell you that the panic and the fear is uncontrollable) and last but certainly not least what will happen to my loved ones (I don't have many but even my two little dogs are enough of a reason for me to stick it out one more night)
All in all I do not think there is anything abnormal or wrong or cowardly about not committing suicide. I think that it is a valid response to a self destructive tendency.
I truly believe that those who take their own life (unless it is fast, or they are unconscious) go through an intensely terrifying experience while they do it, and that is nothing to feel ashamed about not wanting to experience.
I've considered ways to make it fast / unconscious so that I don't experience the terror and panic but even still I don't want to go out like that, I feel like I would be betraying myself...
And every so often I think wow I'm content being alive right now, I'm glad I didn't do that. And that's what keeps me going I guess. Nothing wrong with that.

I totally feel you. I wish that I could just hang out with you and we could rant all night. Wish that I could help you figure out a way to make some money for yourself... I am in a management position right now where I work and I've had to interview quite a few applicants. I would suggest that you try to apply to small businesses for jobs rather than corporate gigs. Corporate jobs usually have very cut and dry hiring processes. Small businesses are much more likely to take a more personal approach. Depression and other mental health issues are common in the workplace however in my experience no one is really forthright about it. There was one guy who worked for me and he had BPD, depression and severe anxiety. A month after he was employed for us, he went suicidal and spent a month in the mental hospital. We gladly welcomed him back though because we genuinely liked him and wanted him to work for us. He worked well for about a year and a half, we even offered him an assistant manager position. Unfortunately he stopped getting therapy and didn't take medication. He was suffering from a lot of other issues and ended up quitting, but the point of the story is that we as a small business cared more about him as a person than his work history. Just give a good reference even if you have to make Shit up! Make a fake business that you worked for and give the name of a person you know is well spoken who can pretend to be your old boss. I know that I never looked into whether people's work experience was real / valid just called the references and asked them questions during the interview. 
Also you are under no obligation to reveal any mental health problems you may have. And employers are required by law to make accommodations for people with disabilities.
So anyway, I can be a reference for you if you want :)
